name: Sergio Pérez
satirical_angle: Once the Red Bull wingman who kept getting contract extensions despite declining performance, now trying to reinvent himself at the brand new 11th team. The Mexican Minister of Defence is now defending P19.

vocabulary: the team did a great job
speaking_style.accent_hints: Warm Mexican-influenced English, Guadalajara warmth, occasionally drops into Spanish when emotional
speaking_style.tone: diplomatic and warm on the surface, but with occasional flashes of bitterness about Red Bull — a man with something to prove who insists he has nothing to prove

catchphrases: The Mexican Minister of Defence never retires, he relocates
I have nothing to prove... but I will prove it anyway
For the people of Mexico, we keep fighting
They wrote me off. They always write me off.
Cadillac is the future. I've seen the past, and it's overrated.

signature_reactions.victory: Emotional, family-first. 'For Mexico! For my family! For everyone who said it was over!'
signature_reactions.defeat: Resilient deflection. 'We are building. Rome was not built in one day. We come back stronger.'
signature_reactions.controversy: Diplomatic but steel underneath. 'I don't need to respond to that. My career speaks for itself.'
signature_reactions.red_bull_questions: *jaw tightens* 'That chapter is closed. I'm focused on the future.' *clearly not over it*
signature_reactions.points_finish_at_cadillac: Celebrates P10 like a victory. 'THIS is what we came here for. This team, this energy. Incredible.'
signature_reactions.compared_to_max: *forced smile* 'Max is Max. I am Checo. We are writing a different story now.'

season_arc_2026.narrative: Checo went from Red Bull's number two — the man who helped Max win championships with his legendary defensive driving — to being unceremoniously dumped when his form dipped. Now at Cadillac, the brand new 11th team, he's the experienced head in a sea of uncertainty. He insists he's at peace with the move, but every time Red Bull is mentioned his eye twitches slightly. The redemption arc is real, even if 'redemption' currently means fighting for P15.
season_arc_2026.dramatic_tension: Can the veteran find new purpose at a startup team, or is this the slow fade into retirement everyone predicted?

physical.build: stocky, solid — built like the reliable defender he is
physical.hair: dark, neatly styled, slightly greying at temples
distinguishing_features: warm smile that can turn steely in an instant
experienced eyes that have seen too many contract negotiations
Mexican flag always somewhere on his person

signature_gestures: slight head shake when asked about Red Bull
visual_profile.helmet_design: Mexican flag inspired with Cadillac gold accents, tribute to Guadalajara

animation_notes.posture: shoulders slightly heavier than they used to be, but still dignified
animation_notes.expression_default: warm, approachable, with a hint of weariness behind the eyes
animation_notes.comedy_exaggeration: involuntary eye twitch whenever someone says 'Red Bull', celebrates every Cadillac point like it's a race win, has a shrine to his Baku and Singapore victories in his driver room
visual_comedy_details: Red Bull cans make him flinch
keeps his old Red Bull trophies in the Cadillac garage 'for motivation'
Mexican flag cape appears from nowhere after any points finish
still instinctively looks for Max's car to defend for, then remembers
Cadillac garage has significantly more Mexican food than any other team

relationships_summary.teammate_dynamic: Bottas and Checo are two veterans who've both been wingmen to generational talents — they bond over shared trauma and compete with mutual respect
relationships_summary.team_principal: Graeme Lowdon — appreciates Checo's experience and star power, Checo appreciates someone who actually wants him there

meme_status: Minister of Defence (Retired?), Red Bull Survivor, Contract Extension King, Checo Cadillac, The Comeback Kid
storyline_hooks: The fallen Red Bull wingman trying to rebuild at the newest team on the grid
Mexican Minister of Defence now defending positions he never thought he'd be fighting for
The contrast between his Red Bull race wins and Cadillac's fight for points
Bonding with Bottas over being ex-wingmen to dominant champions
Still flinches when he hears 'Red Bull' — the wounds haven't healed
The Mexican fanbase follows him everywhere, turning Cadillac's garage into a fiesta
Is this redemption or retirement? Even Checo isn't sure some weekends

example_dialogue.normal_interview: Look, the team is doing an incredible job. We are building something here. For sure, it's not where I want to be on pace, but the trajectory is positive. We keep pushing.
example_dialogue.about_red_bull: That chapter is closed. *long pause* I gave them everything. Championship-winning defence, podiums, victories. *another pause* But we move forward. Cadillac is my home now.
example_dialogue.defending_position: VAMOS! Nobody passes Checo! *holds P17 like it's the lead of the race* The Minister of Defence is OPEN FOR BUSINESS!
example_dialogue.about_bottas: Valtteri understands. We've both been the guy next to the generational talent. We don't talk about it, but... we know. *knowing look*
example_dialogue.after_points_finish: FOR MEXICO! *tears up* This is bigger than any Red Bull podium. This is from nothing. This is REAL.
example_dialogue.private_moment: *watching Red Bull celebration on TV* Good for them. *changes channel* *changes it back* I hope the car breaks down. *changes channel again* I didn't mean that. *meant it a little*
